dossier.public_summary: The dip repeats every 1.58 days exactly as the star itself spins, with the star varying by 2% at that period — much stronger than the 0.6% dip — and the dip depth changes from ~1.5% to ~0.8% between sectors as spots evolve. Depth scatter and a large phase-curve swing are typical of stellar activity, not a stable planet. So the signal is best explained as a spot/spotted-star artefact, not a planet.

reasons.why: Dip is exactly at the stellar rotation period in every sector with huge variability amplitude. Lomb-Scargle amplitudes are 42988-59421 ppm, 7-13x the transit depth 5970 ppm and 2.0% of flux, indicating the star is strongly spotted and the dip is locked to rotation phase. This favours a spot modulation (or spot-crossing artefact) over a planet.

Large out-of-transit swing at this period with amplitude 77% of the dip depth and chi2 576.3/9 is expected for a close binary or for spots rotating in phase with the dip, not for a planet. Planet size is 3.223 Rearth but the light curve is dominated by variability.

Depth changes by a factor >5, especially sector 76 depth 1507 +/-731 ppm vs sector 50 8279 +/-990 ppm. sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source p_constant_all 2.503828733670585e-09 within one source TESS-SPOC, so not a calibration offset. True astrophysical or spot-driven variation.

Individual transits are inconsistent at extreme significance, as expected if the dip depth is modulated by evolving spot coverage at the rotation period. A real planet with this SNR 32.6 should be steady.
reasons.value: 79 transits, p_consistent 4.6539723290930576e-10, chi2 180.16 dof 78, mean_depth_ppm 5649, share_of_top_3 0.112

reasons.why: Transit is longer than central for the M-dwarf size, with high impact parameter and a large density mismatch penalty. Combined with the flat-bottom V shape (v_sigma -3.863, ingress fraction 0.1) and residual scatter, shape and duration do not positively favour a planet despite no secondary (snr -0.7577) or odd-even (diff_sigma 0.5252) or on-target centroid (verdict on_target offset_sigma 1.642). xgboost planet_rank 0.1 supports EB/stellar false positive.
reasons.value: duration ratio 1.552 (observed_h 1.747 vs central_h 1.126), b 0.8784, fit_log_density_ratio -2.565, star_density_penalty 1188, star_density_penalty_share 0.6331, Gaia radius 0.4428612291812897 vs TIC 0.3819

reasons.why: Rules out a neighbour EB (centroid on_target, no plausible blend) and odd/even and secondary rule out a binary on target at twice period. That leaves on-target variability — spot signal — as the best explanation consistent with all checks.
